hints: Focus on the ester link, $\text{RCOO}\text{R'}$, and remember the total carbons in R plus R' must add to 4.
Start with the smallest acid part, methanoate ($\text{HCOO-}$), which leaves 3 carbons for the alcohol part to give two different structures.
Now work through the next combinations, ethanoate with a 2-carbon alcohol and propanoate with a 1-carbon alcohol, then add them all up.
walkthrough:
**Recall what an ester looks like**

Think of an ester as an acid part joined to an alcohol part through the $\text{COO}$ group.

General form:
$$\text{R-C(=O)-O-R'}$$

**Split the 4 carbons between the two sides**

The $\text{C=O}$ carbon counts as part of the acid side. So if acid side has n carbons, alcohol side has (4 - n) carbons.

Possible splits are: 1 + 3, 2 + 2, 3 + 1.

**Draw each case systematically**

Case 1, methanoate (1 carbon acid) + 3 carbon alcohol: $\text{HCOOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{HCOOCH(CH}_3)_2$. That is 2 isomers.

Case 2, ethanoate (2 carbon acid) + 2 carbon alcohol: $\text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$. That is 1 isomer.

Case 3, propanoate (3 carbon acid) + 1 carbon alcohol: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_3$. That is 1 isomer.

**Count them up**

Total = 2 + 1 + 1 = 4 esters. This matches the idea that propyl and isopropyl give the extra isomer many students miss.

options.A: 2 is too low. This usually comes from counting only $\text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_3$ and forgetting the two methanoate isomers.
options.B: 3 is too low. This often happens when you count only one of the propyl methanoate isomers and miss that propyl can be straight chain or branched ($\text{isopropyl}$).
options.C: 4 is correct. The four esters are propyl methanoate, isopropyl methanoate, ethyl ethanoate and methyl propanoate. This covers all 1+3, 2+2 and 3+1 splits of the 4 carbons.
options.D: 5 is too high. This trap comes from including a carboxylic acid isomer such as butanoic acid ($\text{C}_3\text{H}_7\text{COOH}$), which has the same formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}_2$ but is not an ester.
